Yeah you're right, I'm not rooted but it was more of a thought that popped in my head.

I've almost exclusively used Android devices, but my girlfriend is an Apple person. So since I'm a little Android biased I'll tell you what I know from experience.

Rooting is incredibly useful, if you have a need for it. My advice would be to forget the stuff that simply changes the way your phone looks - there are a ton of launchers and widget apps and whatnot for Android that do that well enough without rooting. The end result is generally just a polished turd that looks good one moment and broken the next. Depending on what you mess with you could make updating your phone a nightmare unless you're really willing to take the responsibility to learn how your device really works and update it manually. You can even back up the apps and data on your device these days without root, which was difficult before and required apps like Titanium Backup, which is awesome, but has a learning curve steeper than most apps to use properly.

So, now that I've pissed all over your parade, let me mention the benefits of going through the rooting process and why I've always done it. In the past it was solely so I could back up the apps and data on my phone and install entirely new operating systems. I like to tinker, and Android devices tend to be far less locked down than iOS devices. I'm also a pretty dedicated Tasker user, and with the Secure Settings plugin, which requires root, there's very little you can't customize in terms of automation and device behavior. Want your phone to prompt you if you'd like to open your garage door whenever you pull into your driveway? I do, and I did that with Tasker and Secure Settings. Anyway, I've also leaned towards rooting so that I can keep up with Android updates beyond where my phone's manufacturer has left it behind - something that is far more of an issue with Android devices than it is with iOS devices, but understandably so. I use AdAway, which does a great job of eliminating those annoying advertisements in free apps. Drivedroid lets me use my phone as if it were a bootable USB flash drive to boot one of several operating systems on a PC from my phone - amazingly handy for PC recovery. I use FolderSync to synchronize data on my phone with my home server. All of these things require root to function properly, and in total they're worth the hassle come update time and OTA doesn't work anymore.

So, before you go down the road of root, or get all envious of your coworkers iPhones, check out things like Nova Launcher and Zooper, etc. and pimp out your phone without rooting it. Then, if you get the itch to go further, root that thing and make it do your bidding.

There are some interesting things based on IPv6 out there; like CJDNS system (it's apparently a combination mesh-net, and next hop encrypted routing system); and it's test network Hyperboria.

If enough people ran something like a consumer-grade, highly distributed system that was built with technologies like that those, and combined it with some kind of mesh-net "ProxyHam"; then as long as you are "behind" the device; it would be like having a network of "tor hidden services" or I2P eepsites. Basically, in fantasyland, the hardware router/firewall/cable box that everyone would get by default would be a do all those things (firewall, link to New Hyperboria / HyperboriaTor/I2P, become a mesh-net node for the surrounding few miles, etc..) then it would be a lot safer on the "LAN side", as most of the traffic would be highly protected.

Then one's privacy would be more based on each individual server (and how much data you want to give it), and how well secured your browser is on the client side. It's a lot harder to track everything; when each endpoint needs to be targeted, vs simply copying everything in the clear at various chokepoints.
